## Summary of changes

**New identity key.** `OwnerMapper.identityKey(owner)` now returns the lower-case SHA-256 hex digest (64 hex chars) of `normalizedTelephone + '|' + lowerEmail + '|' + soundex(lastName)`, replacing the old plaintext `telephone|email|householdId`.

**New helper class** `mapper/OwnerIdentity.java` holds `sha256Hex(...)` and an American `soundex(...)` implementation. I put these in a standalone utility rather than as `default` methods on the `@Mapper` interface because MapStruct treated the `String -> String` defaults as ambiguous candidate property-mapping methods (which broke the build).

**Soft-match redesign.** `assignPossibleDuplicate` now flags a possible duplicate when an existing non-deleted owner has the **same postcode** and **same last-name Soundex** but a **different identity key** (previously: same normalized last name + same postcode + different telephone). Because telephone is part of the identity key, two owners with the same last name and postcode but different telephones no longer collide on the key — they are admitted as a soft match instead of a hard 409.

**Duplicate detection (409)** in `rejectDuplicateIdentity` is unchanged in structure — it still compares the single `identityKey`, still skips soft-deleted owners, and the email-domain blocklist still runs first (in `normalizeEmail`, before the check). The separate household-duplicate 409 was already consolidated into this single key; `householdId` is still computed for household size / membership-cap but no longer feeds the identity key.

I also removed the now-unused `toE164OrNull` helper and refreshed the Javadoc in the controller, `DuplicateOwnerIdentityException`, and `ExceptionControllerAdvice` to describe the new key format.
